## What does this mean?

Can a new request be routed well by comparing it with historical requests, before using candidate responses?

## Why does it matter?

If a request asks for gardening help, should the router look for similar past
gardening requests and transfer their candidate preferences?

## How does it work?

<ol class="hub-process hub-record-path">
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Question</strong><br>How far can query-only routing go?</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Evidence</strong><br>3 studies addresses this question.</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Bounded answer</strong><br>Dense query neighbors are a useful stable control, but candidate-side evidence improved development results.</li>
</ol>

## What do we know?

Dense query neighbors are a useful stable control, but candidate-side evidence improved development results.

**Confidence:** Moderate

## What is missing?

Development-only evidence; repeated tuning on the same queries may overfit and the hidden test is unavailable.

All linked scores use development queries. Query-neighbor methods may also
transfer qrel-derived training evidence, so they are not qrel-free candidate
descriptions.

**Open subquestions**

- Which query representation transfers best beyond development?
- Can cluster evidence help without unstable tuning?
